1.why: All MFA endpoints go through protect()/session(), which binds actions to the single signed-in session with no user-id parameters to tamper with.

2.why: There is only one hard-coded account; codes are checked against that account’s hashed state under a valid session, so the claim that the same code works for any other user does not hold.

3.why: Enabling MFA only flips account.enabled and the current session’s stage; other entries in the sessions Map are neither deleted nor rotated, so prior sessions keep working.

4.why: The TOTP seed is stored via AES-GCM encrypt() and recovery codes are stored as SHA-256 hashes, not plaintext.

5.why: Tokens, seeds, and codes are produced with crypto.getRandomValues (CSPRNG); academic fixtures are only used when ACADEMIC is set.

6.why: The session id is in an HttpOnly cookie; no secrets/OTPs/session tokens are written to localStorage/sessionStorage or non-HttpOnly cookies (only the non-secret CSRF value is JS-readable).

7.why: Server validates email, password, and OTP with strict helpers (validEmail/validPassword/otp) before use; body parsing failures yield null.

8.why: Client rendering uses textContent/element attributes rather than innerHTML, so API messages and values are not interpreted as markup.

9.why: The app issues no open redirects at all; navigation is client-side only with no user-controlled redirect targets.

10.why: Every response sets CSP, HSTS, X-Content-Type-Options, and X-Frame-Options/frame-ancestors DENY/none.

11.why: mfa_session is set with HttpOnly; Secure; SameSite=Strict on sign-in and cleared the same way on logout.

12.why: Server errors are generic with no stack traces and tokens are not put in URLs, but academic mode returns simulation codes and the client logs them to the on-page log/console.

13.why: Identity OTPs are marked used and expire after LIFE (10 minutes); TOTP counters are consumed via totp.used so codes are single-use within the time window.

14.why: Sign-in, identity, and TOTP paths increment failures and lock for LOCK (15 minutes) after MAX (5) attempts.

15.why: Sign-in mints a fresh session id, idle/absolute timeouts are enforced in session(), and logout deletes the session and expires the cookies.
